title: Split the R439 literal K defect into target reads and helper wraps across nine words (no new κ)
body:
## Result (finite certificate on nine named words; no new κ)

New package `research/r439-target-closed-k-residual/` (card `bit-helper-contract`, scope refined). It splits the literal `K_equals_D` defect on nine pinned R439 D words from four lineages into two parts. One part is carried by target-to-target reads (`T = N* + N`). The other is the residual left by helper-to-helper gates (`H = K + N*`). Here `N*` is the named mask with `D` replayed and every helper-to-helper gate skipped.

| word | literal \|K+N\| | \|T\| | residual \|H\| | residual sectors = donors | sectors passing after closure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PR915 target basis (no helper gates) | 17,095 | 17,095 | **0** | 0 | 439 |
| PR926 pairs | 17,485 | 13,148 | 7,447 | 192 | 247 |
| PR941 matching / floor | 17,514 / 17,505 | 13,008 / 12,885 | 7,786 / 7,776 | 199 / 199 | 240 / 240 |
| helper triples | 17,541 | 12,444 | 8,685 | 232 | 207 |
| PR1062 pair control | 17,504 | 13,110 | 7,424 | 188 | 251 |
| PR967 stars / PR1062 composition | 17,636 | 12,275 | 8,767 | 221 | 218 |
| PR1062 candidate | 17,653 | 12,092 | 9,163 | 236 | 203 |

- The helper-free PR915 base already carries a 17,095-bit literal defect across all 439 sectors. Target-read closure removes all of it (`K = N*` exactly).
- On all eight helper-mixing words, the residual support is exactly the set of donor helpers, meaning helpers read by some helper-to-helper gate. On the star words these are the 221 / 236 star leaves.
- So #4092's "every sector is defective" reading comes from target reads. After closure, 203–251 sectors per word pass the sector-local test.
- `E = K` and helper restoration hold on all nine words, which extends the `r439-k-cross-term-tally` certificate from three words to nine.
- Control: with a restored wrap and a wrong `K`, `K = N*` reports zero residual while `E ≠ K`. So `K = N*` alone is **not** a sound replacement check once helper gates exist.

## Correction to PR #4092 (same author)

#4092's README says the #3904 pair (target register 112, helper register 260) is not in the official W0 defect set. That is wrong. It mixed register numbers with indices: register 260 is helper index 38, and sector 38's 57 defective targets include target index 1 (register 112). Running #4092's own `verify.py --json` shows this. #3904 and #4092 therefore agree on that bit. #4092's totals, sector counts and controls are unaffected. Its files are not edited here. A verifier control pins the corrected fact.

## Reproduce

From the repository root:

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B research/r439-target-closed-k-residual/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-target-closed-k-residual
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/r439-target-closed-k-residual --check-source-history
```

Local results on CPython 3.12:
- `PASS_R439_TARGET_CLOSED_K_RESIDUAL words=9 pr915_residual=0 star_residual=8767/8767/9163 sectors_equal_donors=9/9 controls=6 no_new_kappa`, about 0.1 s.
- `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.
- `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS` (`--check-only`).
- `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` with source history.

The verifier was also run with `-I -O -Werror`. It uses the standard library only, and all nine inputs are SHA-256 pinned.

## Limitations

This is a finite certificate on nine words. It adopts no replacement for `K_equals_D` or H2, and the 612 target-to-target reads remain a literal H2 read-kind failure. Frames, native schedules, hosted invoices, all-size transfer and supplier admission are not addressed. The selected frontier is unchanged. No independent human or formal review is claimed.

## Open next questions

1. Can a donor-sector contract replace `K_equals_D` on these words? The candidate is `K = N*` plus the donor columns delivered while each restored wrap is open. First step: state it for well-nested restored wraps and test it on the nine words and the six controls. Adopting it is a maintainer policy decision.
2. Does PR915's semantic substitution proof already cover target-read closure, so the 612 reads need no separate H2 repair?

## Related open work

- #3904 (one D-inclusive target/helper pair on the PR967 word): same object. Its pair agrees numerically with this package. The bit is set in `K` and absent from `N` and `N*`, checked by control 6.
- #3533 (abstract three-gate restored edge): same mechanism. Control 2 is that shape; its residual is the single donor column.
- #2721 (H2-F framed transfer without the no-target-feedback clause): related clause, framed level. There is no overlapping number to compare.
- #3891 (abstract q-target helper wrap microinstance): related wrap shape on a six-register instance, not a pinned word. There is no overlapping number.

## CI notes

- `plan`: pass. `replay (research/r439-target-closed-k-residual)`: pass (1m12s). This is the package's registered replay.
- `finite` (workflow `community-batch952.yml`, "Community T37-era finite circuits and bounds"): **fail, not caused by this PR**. The workflow is triggered by any `research/r439-*/**` path. It fails inside `research/central-factor-packed/verify.py` with `ValueError: Source pin mismatch: certificates/dyadic-central-factor.json`. This PR touches neither file. The same job failed with the same error on the run for #4092. Every `pull_request` run of this workflow since 2026-10-19 17:22 UTC has failed (six runs, including those for the merged `r439-k-cross-term-tally` package and an `r439-shear-compensation` branch). Open #4110 repins those central-factor-packed sources. To avoid overlapping it, this PR does not include that repin.
